name: Google Spanner
model: Tables of rows with SQL in GoogleSQL or PostgreSQL dialect; also graph queries (Spanner Graph), full-text and vector search
engine_note: Google's distributed store: data split by key range into splits, each replicated with Paxos across zones or regions; TrueTime clocks order commits
consistency: Multi-row, cross-shard, cross-region transactions. Default serializable with external consistency (the strongest: commit order matches real time); repeatable read (snapshot isolation) is an option. Strong reads are current; stale reads at a chosen timestamp are opt-in.
scaling: Automatic sharding by key range; add compute (nodes or processing units) and splits rebalance; regional or multi-region configurations; no machine sizing.
version_note: Latest dated change read: 2026-09-18, automatic parameterization of SQL query literals; Spanner queues went GA on 2026-09-17.
reach: Reach for it when you need strongly consistent SQL transactions across regions at very large scale and you are on Google Cloud.
avoid: Avoid when the data fits one Postgres server, when you must run outside Google Cloud, or for a small budget (there is a minimum instance cost).
escape: You leave the Postgres default for this because you need global, strongly consistent writes at Google scale.
chat: Users, chats and messages for a very large global product on Google Cloud.
notes: No Jepsen analysis. Isolation facts quoted from the isolation-levels page (2026-10-04); when repeatable read went GA was not stated there. Engine set to 'other' (Google's own storage, described in the 2012 OSDI paper as Bigtable-like; current docs do not name the on-disk format). No sign of a self-hosted Spanner in the current release notes. Stale reads described from the timestamp-bounds page title, not read in full.
